sources.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash model card
sources.evidence: Identifies Gemini 3.8 Flash, published September 2, 2026, as based on 3.7 Flash and explicitly directs architecture questions to its card. Describes API/product distribution under Google terms; no total or active parameter count.

sources.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash API model reference
sources.evidence: Stable model code gemini-3.8-flash; 1,048,576 input tokens; text, image, video, audio and PDF inputs; text output; thinking at low/medium/high levels and function calling supported. Page updated October 22, 2026.

sources.title: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.8 Flash Cyber
sources.evidence: September 2, 2026 launch announcement introduces standard Gemini 3.8 Flash separately from the restricted Flash Cyber variant.

sources.title: Gemini 3.7 Flash model card
sources.evidence: The architecture section explicitly directs readers to the Gemini 3.6 Flash model card.

sources.title: Gemini 3.6 Flash model card
sources.evidence: The architecture section explicitly directs readers to the Gemini 3.5 Flash model card.

sources.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash model card
sources.evidence: The architecture section explicitly directs readers to the Gemini 3 Flash model card.

sources.title: Gemini 3 Flash model card
sources.evidence: The architecture section says 3 Flash is based on Gemini 3 Pro and refers to the Pro model card for architecture.

sources.title: Gemini 3 Pro model card, updated May 2026
sources.evidence: Architecture endpoint of the explicit reference chain: sparse mixture-of-experts Transformer with multimodal inputs. Explains routing each token to a subset of experts, but supplies no numeric total or active count.

sources.title: Developer's guide to Gemini 3.8 Flash
sources.evidence: Places 3.8 Flash within the Gemini Flash line. Its exact-name comparison table confirms stable model ID, context and thinking levels; no model-size row or parameter counts.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon model card
sources.evidence: Later October 13, 2026 model card checked for retrospective disclosure. It provides no total or active parameter count for Gemini 3.8 Flash. Its own architecture is not transferred to this model.

sources.title: Gemini API Additional Terms of Service
sources.evidence: Service access is governed by Google API and Gemini additional terms, including restrictions on extracting or replicating model weights; supports proprietary API-access classification.

sources.title: Models.dev Gemini 3.8 Flash record
sources.evidence: Baseline lead records the stable identifier's release date and capabilities. Technical claims were checked against Google's model card and API documentation.

sources.title: Gemini API release notes — September 2, 2026
sources.evidence: The dated September 2 entry explicitly records the GA release of gemini-3.8-flash.

name.note: Official name for the stable gemini-3.8-flash API identifier; not Flash Cyber.

developer.note: Google DeepMind model published and served by Google; preserves the catalog's Google developer label.

family.note: Google's developer guide explicitly places this model in the Gemini Flash line; normalized catalog family key.

release_date.note: Dated first-party launch announcement introduces this standard variant on September 2; the model card carries the same date.

open_weights.note: Official distribution is through Google products and APIs under service terms, with no public weight distribution offered.

license.note: Descriptive classification for Google's restricted service access, not an open-weight license or the documentation page's content license.

parameters_b.note: No numeric total for the exact 3.8 Flash model is disclosed in its card, the referenced architecture cards, current specification comparison, or later Argon card checked. Exact-name parameter, training and interpretability searches found no first-party size disclosure.

active_parameters_b.note: No numeric active parameter count is disclosed for 3.8 Flash in the checked primary sources. Sparse routing does not establish an active count or justify copying any predecessor's size.

architecture.note: The 3.8 card explicitly refers architecture to 3.7, then 3.6, then 3.5, then 3 Flash, then 3 Pro. The endpoint card specifies sparse MoE Transformer architecture. This follows the documented architecture references; no sibling size or expert counts are assumed.

context_window.note: Google documents 1,048,576 as the input token limit; maximum output is separately 65,536.

modalities.note: Exact stable-model reference lists these supported data types; PDF is retained as a supported input format.

reasoning.note: Thinking is explicitly supported with low, medium and high levels; minimal is unsupported.

description.value: Google's multimodal reasoning model based on Gemini 3.7 Flash, with text output, configurable thinking levels, and function calling.
description.note: Replaces the promotional intelligence superlative with documented lineage, modalities, thinking controls and function calling.

patch.description: Google's multimodal reasoning model based on Gemini 3.7 Flash, with text output, configurable thinking levels, and function calling.

patch.notes: Architecture is supported by the model cards' explicit reference chain: 3.8 Flash → 3.7 Flash → 3.6 Flash → 3.5 Flash → 3 Flash → 3 Pro (sparse MoE Transformer). Total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed in the checked primary sources. The context figure is the documented input limit.

summary: Confirmed the stable standard Gemini 3.8 Flash variant, September 2, 2026 release, Google/Flash identity, hosted access, 1,048,576-token input limit, modalities, thinking and function calling. Added proprietary classification and MoE architecture using the explicit model-card reference chain; replaced promotional description. Total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed after checking referenced cards, an exact-name specification comparison, the later Argon card, and exact-name research searches.
